children: Nomura has maintained its positive stance on the Indian steel sector, saying domestic steelmakers are well positioned to benefit in the first half of FY27 from recent price hikes, which it believes are more than sufficient to absorb raw material cost inflation.The brokerage retained its 'Buy' recommendations on Tata Steel, JSW Steel and Jindal Steel.In its weekly steel trends report dated November 1, Nomura said domestic hot-rolled coil (HRC) prices in India declined Rs 50 per tonne week-on-week to Rs 63,650 per tonne in the week ended October 30, remaining elevated near their highest levels in the past four years.In contrast, rebar prices rose Rs 150 per tonne week-on-week to Rs 64,800 per tonne, extending their recovery after a period of moderation since the first quarter of FY27.The movement in prices has narrowed the domestic flat-long spread in favour of long products, with the differential turning negative at minus Rs 1,150 per tonne as rebar prices gained momentum and outpaced HRC prices.India's HRC spot margin stood at around Rs 39,073 per tonne in October 2026, up around Rs 3,000 per tonne quarter-on-quarter from the second quarter of FY27 and Rs 1,550 per tonne month-on-month.Globally, China's export HRC prices remained unchanged week-on-week at $505 per tonne, while domestic HRC prices declined $2 per tonne to $482 per tonne. Export margins fell $2 per tonne to $205 per tonne, while domestic margins declined by the same amount to $138 per tonne, amid lower realisations and easing global coking coal prices.In Europe, HRC prices remained steady at 750 euros per tonne, with margins unchanged at 482 euros per tonne, partly benefiting from easing global coking coal costs.

Imported coking coal prices remained stable week-on-week at $266 per tonne, around 3 percent below the September 2026 average, indicating some easing in global input cost pressures following a sharp rally.Domestic Chinese coking coal prices also remained unchanged at $338 per tonne, although they have risen more than 40 percent since a fatal mine accident in the country.Global iron ore prices remained weak at $87 per tonne, their lowest level in calendar year 2026 so far. Meanwhile, NMDC raised lump prices by Rs 150 per tonne to Rs 5,400 per tonne with effect from September 2026, while fines prices remained unchanged at Rs 4,500 per tonne.Among non-ferrous metals, LME aluminium spot prices rose around 1 percent week-on-week to $3,105 per tonne, while SHFE aluminium prices were broadly flat at 23,780 yuan per tonne. Copper prices remained elevated at $14,579 per tonne.

title: India steel prices stay elevated as rebar outpaces HRC; Nomura remains positive on sector, retains 'Buy' on Tata Steel, JSW Steel
